blocks.text: These are lifelong mental disorders, which may have an episodic, variable courses. The presenting episodes may be manic, hypo manic, depressive or mixed. By definition, a diagnosis of bipolar disorders requires either a current or previous episode of mania or hypomania.

blocks.text: A manic episode is characterized by a period of time, of at least 1 week, during which the individual has persistent elevated (extreme happiness) or irritable mood and present for most of the days.

blocks.text: In addition, the individual needs to have at least 3 (4 if mood is only irritable) of the following symptoms:
Reduction in the need for sleep
Chattier than usual, with increased pressure to talk
Increase in number of activities engaged
Involvement in activities that might have a potential for serious consequences
There must be marked impairments in terms of functioning with the onset of the above symptomatology.
